summary: Explains referencing suboptions with dotted paths in O(), optional list index markers in brackets that are ignored for linking, and that RV() uses the same syntax for return values.
questions: How do I reference a suboption in module documentation?
Can I show a list index in an option reference without breaking the link?
How do I link to a fact returned by another module in docs?

answer_card.title: Referencing suboptions and return values
answer_card.answer_md:
- Suboptions use dots: `O(foo.bar)`.
- You can add list markers like `O(foo[].bar)` or `O(foo[-1].bar)`; anything inside `[ ]` is ignored for the link target but shown in the text.
- `RV()` works the same way for return values, e.g. `RV(ansible.builtin.service_facts#module:ansible_facts.services)`.
